discoveries: GitHub identifies this repository as a fork of rpcpool/yellowstone-grpc, not a separately specified stream protocol.
The visible README documents Geyser gRPC streaming and block reconstruction, including the caveat that reconstructed block entry counts may be zero.
The repository is AGPL-3.0 licensed. No independent feature delta or SYLPH-specific capability was established in this bounded review.
patterns: treat forks as related provenance, not independent-provider corroboration
compare exact commits and schemas before claiming independent implementations
preserve source license with provenance
sources.overlap: SYLPH currently uses @triton-one/yellowstone-grpc 4.0.2, not this server fork. No Helius Yellowstone source code is installed or executed.
risks: a fork of the same protocol is not an independent source for consensus verification
fork-specific patch state and server/client compatibility were not audited
validation: compare pinned fork commit to upstream diff and license obligations before reuse
use separate provider/operator identity for independent evidence
test identical finalized fixtures against distinct infrastructure

discoveries: Anza Kit is the renamed 2.x line of @solana/web3.js and is MIT licensed; the local project currently pins @solana/web3.js 1.98.4 and many Anchor/web3.js-class APIs.

Kit separates RPC, subscriptions, codecs and address/key handling into typed packages; its docs describe explicitly handling failed subscriptions and catching up missed state with a one-shot RPC read.
Kit's general API evolution and documented support for legacy/v0 transaction-message construction do not by themselves establish support for the newer Solana transaction format or fee semantics.
patterns: explicit subscription failure and catch-up
typed codecs and versioned message contracts
migrate incrementally behind adapter boundaries with cross-SDK fixtures
sources.overlap: The project has reconnect/replay logic and typed canonical ingress; it also depends heavily on web3.js v1. A Kit migration would be broad and is not justified as a drop-in fix. The gap-recovery approach is useful as a comparison, while Yellowstone/archive paths carry the chain-completeness workload.
risks: SDK migration could change address, transaction serialization, RPC, signer and Anchor interfaces
version-aware message types do not equal support for all runtime transaction versions
additional SDK dependencies can create duplicate classes/address identity issues
validation: inventory all web3.js v1 imports and runtime class-identity assumptions
test serialization/decoding against byte fixtures for each claimed transaction version
dual-run RPC/subscription results on a fixed fixture set
avoid signer changes without CRITICAL Astra review

discoveries: Feed derives an explicit processingIntent from the source and routes historical repair through canonical processing while keeping live-feed freshness/provider health separated.
The current source latches live ingress queue overflow only for LIVE observations; non-live overflow does not contaminate live health.

Focused tests exercise newer-slot historical replay, rejected historical evidence, legacy isRepair precedence, non-LIVE overflow, stop/drain behavior, historical post-commit retry through canonical DUPLICATE, live provider-health ordering, and queued-input immutability. A live Census-R failure previously stamped SOLANA_WSS as newly validated before the feed halted, while a queued frame could be mutated before the serial worker read it; provider-health refresh now follows both journal commits and queued logs/bytes are snapshotted after capacity admission.
patterns: explicit LIVE versus HISTORICAL_REPAIR state partition
bounded admission with fail-closed live overflow
test shutdown drains accepted work
sources.overlap: The live/historical health partition remains in place. Deterministic failure injections found that a canonical ACCEPTED observation could be marked seen before a subsequent Census-R write failed; the returned receipt hid that incomplete projection and same-process retry was suppressed. Feed now exposes a post-commit warning and retains retryability; a canonical DUPLICATE can finish the Census-R write without affecting live freshness. Provider-health validation was also moved after both journal commits so a failed secondary projection cannot mint a fresh LIVE observation timestamp.
risks: running service may not load current edited source/dist
Census-R remains a secondary in-memory journal in this path; warning/retryability do not establish crash-durable parity
feed healthy predicate still depends on live freshness and stabilization, not historical coverage alone
validation: inject post-canonical Census-R failure, assert warning and retry through canonical duplicate
inject LIVE WSS and Yellowstone Census-R failures and assert no fresh validated-observation timestamp is recorded
mutate caller-owned logs and raw frame after queue admission; assert processing uses the admission-time snapshot
verify live fields/provider health remain unchanged for historical retries
verify current build ID and process snapshot after operator-controlled rollout
continue independent contiguous coverage checks

discoveries: Production append requires durable Store capability, validates the envelope and raw-payload hash, journals an immutable record, and reads back the committed observation identity.
A separate appendStagingBatch path is explicitly staging-only, bounded to 64 rows, and requires an unforgeable staging capability; regular production append remains one event at a time.
Durability tests reject caller-supplied journal authority, serialize sequence assignment, and verify tamper/replay recovery behavior.
patterns: capability-gate staging-only bulk writes
hash raw evidence before canonical serialization
read-after-write verify journal identity
separate source observation from projection acknowledgement
sources.overlap: This is the canonical evidence boundary for the staged feed-recovery path; no duplicate ingress authority was identified in the reviewed portion.
risks: historical/captured observations require provenance and must not be relabeled LIVE
staging capability must remain unavailable to normal composition
journal durability does not prove external source completeness
validation: continue crash/replay/idempotency and raw-hash tamper fixtures
prove staging capability is absent from production composition
compare confirmed block/transaction coverage with independent sources

discoveries: The reconciler classifies missing slot intervals and only shrinks coverage gaps using compatible contiguous-source receipts.
Legacy persisted coverage frontier data without immutable recovery certificates is rejected rather than trusted to advance canonical continuity.
Recovery certificates, bounded pending backfills and provider-generation checks prevent replaced provider work from silently certifying gaps.
patterns: coverage lane and source provenance on slot receipts
immutable certificate before advancing verified coverage
bounded queue and overflow visibility
provider generation fencing
sources.overlap: The current design separates gap recovery from Feed freshness and uses certificate lineage. It does not on its own guarantee recovery throughput can keep up with the advancing chain tip.
risks: verified prefix can remain far behind live finalized tip
filtered slot receipts cannot prove complete block coverage
provider agreement may be correlated or share upstream data
validation: measure sustainable finalized slot throughput and lag
validate exact contiguous ranges against independently operated sources
test restart/checkpoint recovery and bounded overflow
require verified live-tail handoff evidence
